item.title: Architecture
item.description:
Architecture

Three layers, clean boundaries. The engine doesn’t know about parallel execution. The LLM client doesn’t know about pipelines.

On this page: System layers Run loop Handlers Dippin adapter Agent backends Agent tools State & resume LLM client TUI Library API

System layers

Each box: layer name · source path · what it owns.

cmd/tracker
flags · name resolution · TUI · embedded workflows"] Engine["Pipeline Engine
pipeline/
run loop · edge selection · checkpoints · budget guard · steering channel"] Handlers["Handlers
pipeline/handlers
codergen · tool · human · parallel · fan_in · conditional · subgraph · manager_loop"] Backends["Agent Backends
pipeline/backend.go
native · claude-code · acp"] Agent["Agent Session
agent/
turn loop · tool registry · context compaction · episodic memory · verify-after-edit"] LLM["LLM Client
llm/
Anthropic · OpenAI · Gemini · OpenAI-compat · retry · cost estimation"] CLI --> Engine --> Handlers --> Backends --> Agent --> LLM

The engine run loop

Every node is treated the same: execute the handler, evaluate edges, advance. Parallel, subgraphs, human gates — handlers encapsulate it all.

item.title: Built-in Workflows
item.description:
Built-in Workflows

Four pipelines embedded in the binary. Run by name; customize with tracker init.

On this page: build_product ask_and_execute build_product_with_superspec deep_review Run unattended Customize Testing

All four embedded workflows are coding-flavored — they shipped with the binary because they were the original use case. The pipeline framework itself is general: any sequence of LLM calls plus parallel branches plus human gates fits the same .dip shape. RAG, eval, content moderation, agent triage are all doable; we just haven’t shipped opinionated templates for them yet. Pull requests welcome.

v0.76.0

2026-09-19 release notes →

Added

  • Reports lifecycle state to herdr terminal panes. When tracker runs inside a herdr pane (HERDR_ENV=1, with HERDR_PANE_ID and HERDR_BIN_PATH set) it reports its run state to the pane’s agent manager by shelling out to $HERDR_BIN_PATH pane report-agent — working while the pipeline runs, blocked while a human gate waits, idle at the top-level terminal, then release-agent at teardown. Reports use source custom:tracker, agent tracker, and a strictly increasing --seq. blocked is reported only for interactive runs; autopilot, --auto-approve and --webhook-url resolve gates with nobody waiting, so they never block the pane. Detected and wired automatically for both console and TUI runs (new herdr package); a complete no-op outside a pane, and TRACKER_HERDR=0 opts out even inside one. Best-effort by construction: a failed or slow call (2 s timeout) is swallowed and never affects the pipeline, and the CLI is invoked directly (no shell) so gate text cannot inject arguments.
  • Human gates expose their options as structured data (#631). gate_opened (the --json stream and activity.jsonl: gate_default, gate_options), GateAware.BeginGate’s GateInfo, and the --webhook-url POST body now carry the gate’s declared default: and one pipeline.GateOption per routing option (label, choice, target, default, override, restart, meaning), derived from the node’s outgoing edge labels rather than the prompt text. meaning classifies each option as reject / approve / adjust, so consumers (tracker-runner’s web and Slack gate UIs) can delete their prompt-parsing heuristics; the flat choices list is unchanged for older readers. WebhookInterviewer now implements GateAware.

Tooling & verification

  • Shell fixture suites run hermetically under the pre-commit hook. The example-script suites now strip every inherited GIT_* var except GIT_EXEC_PATH before launching a fixture, so the hook’s relative GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_AUTHOR_* no longer leak into the throwaway repos the fixtures create — a relative index path broke git worktree add (its .git is a file), and an inherited author overrode the fixtures’ deterministic commit identity. build_product’s verify_test.sh uv last-resort cases also mask any ambient pytest on PATH so their precondition holds host-independently.
  • Complexity gate skips .scratch/. scripts/complexity/gate.sh now excludes the gitignored .scratch/ tree alongside .worktrees/ and .claude/. Local experiments left there no longer register as phantom new violations; CI never saw them (the tree is gitignored), so this only unbreaks local make complexity.

v0.75.0

2026-09-18 release notes →

Added

  • tracker.ParseSource(source, format, opts...) — parse a pipeline into a *pipeline.Graph without constructing an engine, with the same sidecar resolution Run / NewEngine apply: WithSource(SourceRef{Builtin: name}) resolves prompt_file / command_file from the embed FS and marks the graph as that built-in so NewEngineFromGraph still materializes its ${graph.workflow_dir} tree. The seam an embedder needs to hold and mutate the graph (per-node model tiering, a forced provider) before NewEngineFromGraph for a built-in whose sidecars are not on disk — the path tracker-runner’s force-model bridge takes (runner #906).
  • build_product: dedicated fixture suites for lib/build-context.sh (47 checks) and lib/gate-integrity.sh (79 checks), previously exercised only through the node suites. Pins the seeded build-context.md shape and best-effort contract, and the gate’s restore_gate_files / snapshot_hatch_files / report_hatch_additions behaviour. Found along the way: the build-context Key interfaces grep never matched a Rust pub trait / pub(crate) trait; the visibility prefix is now optional.

Changed

  • build_product / superspec: milestone-scoped cargo test (upstreamed from tracker-runner #901). verify.sh ran the whole unscoped cargo test in milestone mode while go test was already scoped to the changed packages, so a Rust milestone that authored no test still greened on prior milestones’ crates. Every .rs changed since the milestone base (base→worktree: uncommitted edits, untracked files, deletions) now maps to its owning crate (nearest ancestor Cargo.toml with a [package]) and runs cargo test -p <crate>…; no resolvable crate, or --final, tests the whole workspace. Crate names are only ever -p arguments, never eval’d. Fixture suite V14 pins it; superspec’s parity copy re-synced.
  • dippin-lang pinned to v0.76.0 (from v0.73.0, via v0.75.0). The four stopgaps tracker filed in v0.74.0 are retired: #304 — pipeline.ResolveFileDirectivesFS is a thin wrapper over dippin’s parser.ResolveFileDirectivesFS (the tracker mirror is deleted; upstream adds a 4 MiB cap, directory rejection and symlink checks); #306 — dippin simulate honours else ->’s success-side-only contract like the engine; #307 — writable_paths_mode is a typed agent-node / parallel-branch field (the adapter maps it, the legacy params: spelling stays accepted, FinalCommit moves to the typed form); #305 + #315 — DIP125 no longer misreads a ${graph.workflow_dir} body as a binary, knows the : builtin and skips sourced functions, so the three built-ins go from 25 bogus hints to zero and the CLI load path prints hint-severity diagnostics again (the v0.74.0 suppression is removed; a DIP125 regression now shows on every run). The one remaining hint is build_product’s accurate DIP165 on FinalCommit’s deliberate writable_paths_mode: prefer. Also ships the DeepSeek V4.1 repricing (deepseek-flash added, deepseek-v4-pro repriced, V3-era ids marked retired first-party). Golden traces unchanged; all three shipped pipelines stay dippin doctor A/100.

v0.74.0

2026-09-18 release notes →

Added

  • build_product, build_product_with_superspec and ask_and_execute are decomposed into sidecars (#398 follow-up). Every agent prompt: lives in examples/prompts/<name>/<NodeID>.md and every tool command: in examples/scripts/<name>/<NodeID>.sh (POSIX sh), with build_product’s shared shell in scripts/build_product/lib/ sourced via ${graph.workflow_dir}. Pure moves — the resolved IR is byte-identical. Each script has a fixture suite beside it (24 suites, ~900 checks, run under sh and dash by make test-scripts and go test ./...). Embedded built-ins resolve *_file directives from the binary’s embed FS (pipeline.ResolveFileDirectivesFS, a stopgap for dippin-lang#304) and ${graph.workflow_dir} now resolves for them by materializing the tree into <workDir>/.tracker/workflow/<name>/ on every run; tracker init copies the same sidecar set. Library callers anchor a source with tracker.SourceRef{Path | Builtin} (Config.Source / WithSource). Packed .dipx of a decomposed built-in is refused before any node runs.
  • build_product converged with tracker-runner’s battle-tested fork (epic #655). EnsureEnv runs a seed build-setup.sh hook between Setup and SpecLint (env-failed or a missing marker aborts the run — runner #846). verify.sh is deny-by-default: a suite counts as an oracle only on a positive executed-test count (Go === RUN, jest/vitest/mocha/TAP reporters, cargo summaries, pytest collection) and exits 3 NOT-YET-VERIFIABLE when nothing ran — TestMilestone maps it to a tests-not-yet-verifiable marker for VerifyMilestone to decide, while --final stays red unless the operator stamps .ai/build/no-tests-ok (runner #857/#873). Language-native lint (vet / golangci-lint / tsc / eslint / ruff / mypy / clippy) is advisory; only a project Makefile ci/check/lint/test target blocks. The escalate sentinel is __ROUTE_ESCALATE__ (runner #840). Python gets manifest-free discovery and a .venv → venv → pytest → uv run interpreter chain. Decompose declares per-milestone contract tests that TestMilestone reconciles against an executed-test manifest, so a milestone that authors no test can no longer go green on the prior suite (runner #901).
  • writable_paths_mode: prefer (#648). A hardened node jails exactly as today where Landlock is available and otherwise runs UNJAILED with a loud, recorded warning on every surface (jail_degraded event, TUI warning, tracker diagnose / doctor, run.json). Only the host-capability refusal degrades; malformed globs and claude-code / acp backends still refuse in both modes, and in-process Write/Edit/ApplyPatch keep the glob policy via openat2 / os.Root. Default require is unchanged; FinalCommit re-declares its .git/**, .ai/** guard under prefer.
  • tracker -r rewinds past a fail-closed terminal (#651, #654). A run that halted at a fail-routed dead end (AbortRun) resumes at the node that failed, with fail-routing provenance (fallback_origin, outcome, reason, kind) and halted_at persisted on the checkpoint and a resume_rewound event. --from <node> and --resume-no-rewind are the explicit forms; a rewind whose origin is a human gate or a parallel/subgraph node is skipped with a warning.
  • SpecLint advisory rule (i) for evidence-cited under-specification, surfaced at ApprovePlan; docs/build-product-spec-prompt.md is an authoring prompt for the SPEC.md a run consumes.

Changed

  • Unattended build_product runs fail closed. Mechanical tool failures (Setup, a failed milestone pick, CommitIfDirty, …) and pre-build agent failures (ReadSpec, Decompose) route to a new AbortRun terminal instead of the post-build accept gate (#640 A1/A2). A red FinalBuild, failed FinalSpecCheck or reviewer failure reaches a new EscalateVerification gate whose unattended default is abandon → AbortRun; EscalateReview (default accept, audited override: true) is kept only for a green build whose re-review budget is exhausted. Every gate’s abandon now ends the run fail (it previously reached Done and reported success), in ask_and_execute and superspec too. Routing markers are matched with endswith, a CheckVerifyFailBudget breaker caps verify-driven fixes at 3, and EscalateMilestone’s unattended mark done is an audited override (#640 A3–A6).
  • Green means green (#640 D). verify.sh / ci-probe.sh detect every build stack anywhere in the tree and run each in its own directory; the milestone Go scope is base→worktree plus reverse dependencies; known_failures skips are anchored and validated; gate files are re-emitted from the sidecar before every run and hatch-file / operator-stamp additions since milestone start are reported to the verifier; FinalBuild runs --final with -count=1 and fails a Go product with zero test files. Git safety (#640 C): worktree-correct info/exclude, append-if-absent .gitignore seeding, a secrets denylist with private-key sniffing, per-invocation binary excludes, unsigned hook-respecting checkpoint commits and a dirty-tree preflight at Setup (opt-out .ai/build/allow-dirty). State (#640 B/E): Setup and a re-plan reset every per-plan state file, and one shared plan parser in lib/milestones.sh accepts the header and **Files** shapes LLMs actually write. Operator stamps are documented in the README and on the workflows page.
  • Sibling pipelines get the same class of fixes (#646). adversarial-review is dash-safe (its set -o pipefail killed every tool node on Linux); the seven dotpowers workflows anchor task ids and share one scripts/dotpowers/lib/; megaplan sprint ids parse portably; ask_and_execute tests every candidate and parses the winner from a WINNER: contract line; superspec commits its scaffold, folds per-stream traceability overlays mechanically, routes merge conflicts to a gate and uses build_product’s green gate. Fake-green gates (rg missing, no build system) are failures everywhere.
  • ReviewCodex runs gpt-5.6-sol at medium effort with max_turns: 40; ReviewGemini runs gemini-2.5-flash. build_product.dip raises defaults.max_restarts to 200 as the run-wide milestone-count bound (see #643).
  • The CLI load path no longer prints hint-severity dippin diagnostics (DIP125 misreads a ${graph.x} placeholder as the binary -eu — dippin-lang#305); dippin lint still shows them. CLAUDE.md is gotchas + pointers again; the engine spec lives in docs/architecture/engine.md.

Fixed

  • Retry-exhausted fallback_retry_target is a one-shot latch (#642). A fallback path leading back into the failing node cycled forever (1,921 gate prompts in 120 s with zero restarts); a second exhaustion now emits fallback_latched and dead-stops. A writable_paths refuse-to-start is a non-retryable, routable OutcomeFail, and the Landlock requirement is stated as kernel 6.2 (ABI v3) everywhere.
  • Restart budgets are scoped per loop iteration (#643). The engine derives each loop header’s natural loop by dominator analysis and resets the nested targets’ RestartCounts (and re-arms their fallback latches) on every counted restart of the header, so a 60-milestone build no longer dies at max_restarts total. The outermost loop’s max_restarts is the run-wide bound the author sizes. New restart_budget_reset event.
  • Tool timeout: is a routable OutcomeFail (#644), not an unroutable handler error — a slow make ci reaches FixMilestone / EscalateMilestone instead of killing the run. New tool_timeout event and diagnose suggestion.
  • auto_status no longer fails open on realistic STATUS: variants (#645) — trailing punctuation or prose, backticks, emphasis, an unclosed fence. Gate-like prompts emit an early STATUS:fail so a truncated verdict fails closed.
  • Word conjunctions in edge conditions route correctly (#647). Dippin spells and / or / not; tracker split only on && / ||, so a != x and b != y was one always-true clause and the dotpowers task loop could never exit. Conditions are now serialized from dippin’s parsed AST (bounded DNF, negation pushed to leaf operators); Raw is only the fallback.
  • Section-level else -> Node is honored at run time (#649), success-side only, mirroring dippin simulate; every engine graph walk is else-aware.
  • Failure cascade parity (#650, #652, #653). A graph-level on_failure resolving to the failing node is a no-op (no spurious fallback_latched on AbortRun); a failed node whose conditional edges all miss now runs dippin’s documented order (fail edge → retry → fallback_target → on_failure → halt) instead of dead-stopping; tool nodes carry FailureReason (exit code + stderr tail) onto stage_failed, the TUI and tracker diagnose; every failure message says how the node was reached (routed from "Setup" via fail edge).
  • Freeform human gates honour default: under --auto-approve and timeouts. They took the first edge label regardless of the declared default.
  • build_product stack detection dropped every manifest deeper than one directory whenever a first-level one existed (an unquoted glob was expanded by the shell before git ls-files saw it); .venv / venv / site-packages are excluded from manifest detection. A known_failures entry of and / or / not no longer breaks pytest. Stale-file discipline around the tracker-runner #900 symptom: PickNextMilestone removes the previous pick up front so no failing pick can leave a stale milestone for Implement.

Tooling & verification

  • CI: a dedicated jail-linux job on ubuntu-24.04 runs the Landlock jail suite. The Blacksmith runner has no Landlock, so every enforce-path jail test had been silently skipping while reading as green; the job asserts Landlock, requires four literal PASS lines and fails on any Landlock-unavailable skip. workflow_dispatch lets branch CI run on demand. The pre-commit hook’s gotest wrapper drops the GIT_AUTHOR_* / GIT_COMMITTER_* idents git commit exports so script identity assertions pass under the hook.
  • dippin-lang issues filed for this release’s stopgaps, each pinned by a tracker-side parity test: #304 (ResolveFileDirectivesFS), #305 (DIP125 placeholder mis-extraction), #306 (simulate and else ->’s success-side contract), #307 (typed writable_paths_mode).

v0.73.2

2026-09-17 release notes →

Changed

  • dippin-lang pinned to v0.73.0 (dippin #301 / #302) — dippin’s pricing.Lookup now resolves a dated model snapshot id to its undated family price natively. Tracker’s engine-side fold (below) stays as belt-and-suspenders so pricing does not regress to $0 if the upstream fold ever changes.

Fixed

  • Dated model snapshot ids price correctly (#639). A provider-returned id like claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 or gpt-4o-2024-08-06 missed the undated catalog key and priced at $0, leaving turn_metrics estimated_cost, --max-cost, and downstream budget rollups blind. llm/pricing.go now retries a miss once with the trailing -YYYYMMDD / -YYYY-MM-DD suffix stripped — exact catalog match always wins, and a dated id whose family is also unknown still surfaces as unpriced rather than silently $0.

v0.73.1

2026-09-13 release notes →

Fixed

  • OpenAI-compatible streaming completions use a byte-idle deadline instead of the HTTP client’s total timeout. A response that is still producing bytes can now run past five minutes; a silent hang stays bounded and retryable, and an incomplete stream still fails when the [DONE] completion marker is missing. Non-streaming requests keep their configured total timeout.

v0.73.0

2026-09-09 release notes →

Added

  • adversarial-review reusable subgraph (#623). A read-only, parallel adversarial code review that a workflow embeds with ref: — the false-positive control from Adversarial Review (arXiv 2608.18167) shipped as engine structure + deterministic tools, not prompt discipline. examples/subgraphs/adversarial-review.dip runs three independent perspectives (correctness / security / design) in parallel over a frozen diff, merges + cross-perspective dedupes their findings, runs a typed-verdict critic audit, and loops a bounded re-review over contested findings (the graph’s per-target max_restarts is the engine-side bound, enforced before the adjudicate round cap can exhaust it). Final verdicts come from the deterministic FP gate — ungrounded DISAGREE_CONCERN findings are demoted by rank_and_filter.sh, plus the caller’s severity_threshold — and leave via the declared output contract writes: review_findings, review_verdict (callers read ctx.review_findings / ctx.review_verdict and route on approve/rework). The subgraph is read-only by construction: every agent only reads the frozen diff and writes findings JSON under .ai/review/, so a hostile diff cannot steer the reviewers into editing code. Failure is fail-closed at the approval boundary: a review that cannot complete degrades to rework, never approve. examples/adversarial-review-demo.dip is the drop-in caller (subgraph + report node). Scripts live in examples/subgraphs/scripts/adversarial-review/ (moved from the #622 spike location); rank_and_filter_test.sh proves the node gate’s threshold/verdict behavior and lockstep parity with the #622 reference rank_filter.sh on the shared fixture corpus. Both new pipelines pass dippin doctor (A grade) and dippin simulate -all-paths.

v0.72.7

2026-09-08 release notes →

Changed

  • dippin-lang pinned to v0.72.0 (#637 / dippin #297) — openai-compat (alias openai-compatible) is now a first-class custom-gateway provider in dippin’s catalog: every id under it is known-but-unpriced, so loading an openai-compat pipeline no longer surfaces a spurious DIP108 “model not in catalog” warning per agent. Cost estimation follows suit — the new llm.EstimateCostForProvider prices a catalogued id routed through the gateway from the catalog as before, but treats an opaque gateway id as unpriced by design ($0, no “unknown model” diagnostic) rather than a genuine miss; a first-party provider with an uncatalogued id still warns. The token tracker, agent session, and ACP backend cost paths use it.
  • dippin-lang pinned to v0.71.0 (#626 / dippin #296) — uptakes the catalog v0.71.0 pricing refresh; tracker doctor’s PinnedDippinVersion and the Models & Providers table follow. Example pipelines pick up the current stable model ids (#629): claude-sonnet-5 / claude-opus-5 / gpt-5.5 replace the retired claude-sonnet-4-6 / claude-opus-4-6 / gpt-5.2 pins, tiering intact.

Fixed

  • tracker doctor no longer false-fails openai-compat gateway keys (#636). The OpenAI sk- prefix assertion was applied to OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY too, flagging a valid minted JWT / arbitrary bearer as “invalid format” even though runs worked. openai-compat now only requires a non-empty key — the upstream defines its own credential shape. When the key is set but neither OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL nor TRACKER_GATEWAY_URL resolves an endpoint, the OK line carries an advisory hint that requests go to the adapter default (OpenRouter).
  • --backend claude-code could not start: subprocess no longer outlives cancellation (#635). The claude subprocess was spawned with exec.Command, whose cmd.Wait ignores context cancellation — cancelling a claude-code agent left the process (and its children) running and the session turn hung. The spawn now uses exec.CommandContext so a cancelled run kills the subprocess.
  • Operator rejection at a human gate is no longer reported as success (#633). The exit node’s passthrough handler always returns success, so a run that reached the exit after the operator chose the gate’s rejection-labeled (abandon / reject) non-override edge terminated success — the rejection was invisible in result.Status. The exit success path now checks the durable checkpoint edge selections and terminates fail with a run rejected at human gate … message. Accepts (override: true edges) and unlabeled freeform/interview gate→exit edges are unaffected.

v0.72.6

2026-09-04 release notes →

Fixed

  • build_product milestone escalation: accept now escapes the structural gate (#730). When CheckMilestoneOutputs flags a milestone (outputs-missing), the EscalateMilestone gate’s accept choice re-entered CheckMilestoneOutputs — the very check the operator is overriding — so a flagged tree (a false positive on a green build, or a true positive the operator has chosen to ship anyway) deterministically cycled back to the gate until only abandon (discard the whole run) exited. accept now routes forward to ClearStaleReviews, the same ship/review entry the outputs-present edge uses: the run still earns the three-way cross-review, the FinalBuild whole-tree go test ./..., and the FinalSpecCheck compliance subgraph before Cleanup (#392 intent preserved), while accept is always a real forward exit, independent of why the gate flagged.

v0.72.5

2026-09-02 release notes →

Changed

  • dippin-lang pinned to v0.70.0 — Meta joins the catalog as a new provider and the Muse Spark family is priced, so the Models & Providers table now lists five more ids (117 entries across 11 providers): muse-spark-1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3 at $1.25/M in, $0.15/M cached read, $4.25/M out, plus muse-spark-1.2-contributor and muse-spark-1.3-contributor at $0.10 / $0.002 / $0.20. All carry a 1M context window; max_output and capability data are absent by design (Meta publishes no per-version values), so a context-window lookup resolves while capability queries stay unknown — dippin’s absent-not-guessed contract.
  • The -contributor tier is Meta’s own, and it has a string attached. The ~12× cheaper price is bought by granting Meta permission to train on your prompts and completions. Only the standard ids carry family metadata, so a provider-scoped muse-spark@latest resolves to muse-spark-1.3 and can never silently land a run on the train-on-my-data tier.
  • No tracker pricing code changed: the Meta entries carry an absolute cached-input price, so tracker’s cache overlay self-disables for them and the real $0.002/M contributor cache-read rate is billed rather than the 0.1× default’s $0.01/M — a 5× error avoided by construction.
  • Muse is priced, not yet reachable. tracker still has no Meta provider routing, so a Muse model can be costed but not run. Meta describes its Model API as OpenAI-SDK compatible, which makes openai-compat plus a base URL the likely path — unverified against a live endpoint.

v0.72.4

2026-09-02 release notes →

Changed

  • dippin-lang pinned to v0.69.0 — six newly verified models join the catalog tracker prices and lists against (117 entries): claude-fable-5-1, gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.8-flash, glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, MiniMax-M2.5-highspeed. Fable 5.1's unusual 0.025× cache-read rate is honored exactly (tracker's cache overlay self-disables for any model dippin prices), so a cache-heavy run is billed at $0.25/1M rather than the 0.1× default's $1.00. Also picks up dippin's fix to a daily pricing-sync job that reported success while detecting nothing. No tracker code change — the model catalog is derived from dippin by construction.

v0.72.3

2026-08-26 release notes →

Added

  • Deterministic false-positive gate for Adversarial Review (#622 spike) — encodes the paper's typed-verdict control (AGREE/DISAGREE_EVIDENCE/DISAGREE_CONCERN) as a tool: a finding survives only when grounded, ungrounded concerns are demoted. 15-case fixture suite. The full reusable subgraph is #623.

v0.72.2

2026-08-26 release notes →

Changed

  • Fail-safe cost cap on build_product's un-cached ReviewCodex lane (#353) — the OpenAI reviewer (zero prompt-cache reads) was the $7.35-runaway risk and had no bound; now max_cost_usd: 4.00 + cost_exceeded_action: fail routes a breach to the human gate (no retry, no lost work). Conservative floor; the cached Anthropic lane stays uncapped.

v0.72.1

2026-08-26 release notes →

Changed

item.title: CLI Reference
item.description:
CLI Reference

Every command, flag, and resolution rule. Install and operate tracker from the terminal.

On this page: Install Commands Flags Exit codes Tool safety Name resolution Environment variables Autopilot Backends Companion binaries Troubleshooting Diagnose intelligence Quick reference

Install

# Go install (binary includes embedded workflows)
go install github.com/2389-research/tracker/cmd/tracker@latest

# Homebrew
brew install 2389-research/tap/tracker

# Or build from source
git clone https://github.com/2389-research/tracker
cd tracker && make install

# Verify installation
tracker doctor

# Stay current (checks automatically, or run manually)
tracker update

Commands

Running Pipelines

tracker <pipeline>
Run a pipeline. Accepts a file path (build_product.dip, build.dipx), bare name (build_product), or path with slash. .dipx bundles are SHA-256-verified at load time and the bundle identity is threaded through every audit surface. .dipx v0.26.0 Opens TUI dashboard by default.
tracker -r <id> <pipeline>
Resume a previous run by ID. Prefix matching works — -r 7813b is enough if unambiguous. A run that halted at a fail-closed dead end it reached by fail-routing (a node whose only continuation is the exit — e.g. build_product's Setup → AbortRun) rewinds to the node that failed, so fixing the cause and resuming retries that step instead of re-running the terminal. A fail-routed node with real onward routing (a Fix step that loops back to Test) is retried in place. --from <node> re-enters at an explicit node; --resume-no-rewind resumes exactly at the checkpoint's current node.
tracker --no-tui <pipeline>
Run in console mode (no dashboard). Human gates use inline prompts. Auto-selected when stdin is not a TTY.
tracker --json <pipeline>
Stream events as newline-delimited JSON to stdout. Implies --no-tui. For CI/programmatic consumption.

Workflow Management

tracker workflows
List all embedded built-in workflows with display names and goals.
tracker init <name>
Copy a built-in workflow to ./name.dip in the current directory, together with its whole prompts/name/ and scripts/name/ subtrees (including sourced scripts/name/lib/ helpers, minus the *_test.sh fixture suites) plus every file its prompt_file / command_file directives reference elsewhere — the same set an embedded run materializes, so ${graph.workflow_dir} resolves the copy identically (and a starter SPEC.md for workflows that need one). Refuses to overwrite existing files.

Validation & Simulation

tracker validate <pipeline>
Check pipeline structure — parsing, structural validation, semantic validation, lint. Exits 1 on errors. Supports bare names. Accepts .dip, .dot, and .dipx bundles. .dipx v0.26.0
tracker simulate <pipeline>
Dry-run execution plan. Shows nodes, edges, BFS traversal, unreachable nodes, and graph-level attrs (sorted, deterministic). No LLM calls. Supports bare names. Accepts .dip, .dot, and .dipx bundles. .dipx v0.26.0
tracker estimate <pipeline>
Rough pre-run cost & scale ballpark v0.46.0 — prices each agent node's model against a turn heuristic and reports steps, agent-node count, distinct models, and a Low–High cost range with an expected value (e.g. build_product → $0.65–$10.02, expected ~$3.56). No LLM calls; supports bare names. A deliberately wide range — actual cost depends on how many turns each agent uses and how many times loops run.
tracker verify-tests [dir] [--race] [--coverage]
Test-fidelity gate v0.54.0 — scans Go test bodies under dir (default cwd) and flags groups that are byte-for-byte identical or identical except for literal values, so a “distinct” test that copies another's body can't hand out false coverage credit. Exits 1 when any duplicate group is found — drop it into a VerifyMilestone tool node. With --race, also runs go test -race ./... and fails on a detected data race or a suite that won't pass under the race detector; the race pass is opt-in and Go-only — skipped (not failed) when there is no go.mod/go.work or no go toolchain, and reported as a skip when cgo or the race detector is unavailable on the platform. It also prints an advisory v0.69.0 structural near-duplicate report — reordered/renamed copies calling the same production symbols that the literal-strip hash misses — which never affects the exit code. With --coverage, an opt-in, advisory per-test coverage-attribution pass additionally flags tests that execute zero production code (assert on a copy / path guarded out) and test-local functions that re-implement uncovered production logic; it is heavyweight (one go test run per test), Go-only, skips cleanly like --race, and never fails the gate.

Headless & Integration

tracker --webhook-url <url> <pipeline>
Fully headless. Every human gate is POSTed as JSON to <url>; the pipeline blocks until a callback arrives at the local callback server. Slack bots, email approval, mobile push. Mutually exclusive with --autopilot and --auto-approve. v0.17.0
tracker --param key=value <pipeline>
Override a workflow's top-level vars (available as ${params.key}). Repeatable. Unknown keys hard-fail at startup. v0.19.0
tracker --export-bundle <path> <pipeline>
After the pipeline completes, package the full artifact run directory as a portable git bundle (git bundle create --all). Clone with git clone <bundle> on any machine to inspect every commit and checkpoint tag. v0.17.0
tracker --gateway-url <url> <pipeline>
Route every provider through a Cloudflare AI Gateway. Tracker appends the per-provider suffix (/anthropic, /openai, /google-ai-studio, /compat). Equivalent to TRACKER_GATEWAY_URL. Per-provider *_BASE_URL env vars still win. v0.17.0

Autopilot

tracker --autopilot <persona> <pipeline>
Replace all human gates with LLM-backed decisions. Personas: lax, mid (default), hard, mentor.
tracker --auto-approve <pipeline>
Deterministic auto-approval of all human gates. No LLM calls — always picks the default or first option. For CI and testing.

Diagnostics

tracker doctor [pipeline]
Preflight health check. Per-provider API key validation (masked), dippin binary version, .ai/ writability, disk space, .gitignore hygiene, dangerous env var warnings. Live per-provider auth validation with a 1-token call runs by default; pass --probe=false to skip it. Optional pipeline arg runs full lint and warns when a node pins a model that dippin marks retired on its first-party provider API (still billable via a Bedrock/Vertex passthrough) — suppressed when a gateway is configured (TRACKER_GATEWAY_URL/TRACKER_GATEWAY_KIND), since the model then routes to a passthrough. v0.63.0 Exit code 2 on warnings-only. v0.17.0
tracker diagnose [runID]
Deep failure analysis. Reads status.json + activity.jsonl. Shows tool output, stderr, errors, timing anomalies, actionable suggestions (deterministic failure pattern, escalation hit, suspicious timing, budget halt). Without ID, analyzes the most recent run.
tracker status [runID]
Agent-authored high-level timeline of a run #494 — the status updates agents wrote as they worked, in order, for a fast “what happened” read. Without an ID, uses the most recent run.
tracker audit <runID>
Full audit report: timeline, retries, errors, recommendations. For post-hoc analysis of any run.
tracker list
List recent pipeline runs with timestamps, status, and node count.
tracker run-json [runID]
Assemble the run.json manifest for a run directory from its captured audit log — goal, terminal status, per-node kind/attempts/outcome/turns/usage, run totals, tool-call and event counts, and spec identity. v0.50.0 Works after the fact, so a SIGKILLed run (which ran no in-process finalizer) or a run archived before the manifest existed both get one. Without an ID, targets the most recent run.

Setup

tracker setup
Interactive provider configuration wizard. Saves keys to ~/.config/tracker/.env.
tracker version
Show version, commit hash, build time, and configured providers.
tracker update
Self-update to latest release. Downloads from GitHub, verifies SHA256 checksum, smoke-tests the binary, and atomically replaces with .bak rollback. Detects Homebrew and go install and advises accordingly.

Flags

Flags can appear before or after the pipeline argument.

item.title: Glossary
item.description:
Glossary

Terminology used across Tracker pipelines, the Dippin language, and the multi-agent runtime.

On this page: Pipeline & runtime Dippin language Agents & backends Node handlers Routing & outcome Governance Artifacts & inspection

Pipeline & runtime

The core abstractions the engine works with.

Pipeline

A directed graph of nodes connected by edges, plus shared context. Defined in a .dip file and executed by the engine.

Engine

The Tracker runtime that walks the graph: pick a node, execute its handler, evaluate outgoing edges, advance. Treats every node the same — no special-cases for parallel or fan-in.

item.title: How we verify tracker
item.description:
How we verify tracker

tracker is built to be safe to let run unattended. That claim only holds if the engine behaves the same way tomorrow that it does today. Four mechanical gates keep it honest — the centerpiece is a golden-trace conformance suite versioned in lockstep with every release.

On this page: Golden-trace conformance Complexity ratchet Docs-drift gate Provider round-trip tests SWE-bench

Golden-trace conformance

The tracker-conformance binary is the executable snapshot of engine behavior. It runs an example workflow through the real engine with a stub completer — no API keys, no wall-clock or run-id noise — and emits a normalized, deterministic trace: the event sequence, per-node SessionStats, the aggregate UsageSummary, and the terminal status and class.

item.title: Models & Providers
item.description:
Models & Providers

Tracker runs any model through one of three backends, prices every run against a shared catalog, and lets you route traffic straight to a provider or through a gateway. The model list and prices below are derived from dippin-lang (the pinned version) — a single source of truth, so what you see here is exactly what the engine uses to estimate cost and enforce --max-cost.

Backends

Every agent node runs on one backend; you can mix them per node.

item.title: Roadmap
item.description:
Roadmap

A rolling engineering roadmap in thematic workstreams across Now / Next / Later. Priorities, not dates.

The GitHub milestones mirror the Now tier and are the source of truth for what's actively in flight; everything below Now is directional and will churn. Canonical copy lives in ROADMAP.md.

Now

The active milestones — what we're building next.

Failure UX & recovery — epic #493

item.title: Slack Bot
item.description:
Slack Bot v0.46.0

Drive Tracker from Slack. Mention @trackerbot make me an app that… and it starts a pipeline in a thread, streams notifications and clarifying questions to that thread, and delivers the result — arbitrarily many runs at once, each isolated. This page takes you from zero to your first run.

item.title: Transports
item.description:
Transports

A transport is a front-end that drives runs and relays them to a human. The terminal TUI, the Slack bot, a future web or mobile app — every one is a first-class peer on the same small library boundary. None is privileged.

On this page: The boundary Six interactions The interviewer seam Inherited invariants Concurrency The transports Slack: trackerbot Build a transport

The boundary

The core engine knows nothing about LLMs, subprocesses, terminals, or Slack. A front-end plugs in through a small, deliberate library surface — tracker.Config → Engine, an Interviewer seam for human gates, the event streams, and RunManager for concurrency. What the library can do and what the product can do are the same set.
